name: Shun Kee Typhoon Shelter Seafood
area: Causeway Bay (typhoon shelter, ~10 min walk from MTR Exit D4)
cuisine: Cantonese typhoon-shelter seafood on a sampan
intro: You are taken out to an old fishing boat moored in the Causeway Bay typhoon shelter and fed wok-fried seafood on board, a rare surviving piece of old Hong Kong.
must_order: Typhoon shelter crab (deep-fried garlic and chilli)
reviews: Reviewers love the setting and the garlic crab; common complaints are high prices (one diner paid ~HK$1,600 for 4), plastic cups and limited boats.
group_friendly: Booking essential (call or WhatsApp; some guides say pre-order days ahead). There are few boats and they fill up. Seating per boat is unknown (a 2011 blog said about 2–10), so 12 on one boat is unconfirmed: ask whether they can do 12 or split you across two boats. BYO wine; Time Out says closed Wednesdays.
maps_query: Shun Kee Typhoon Shelter Seafood Causeway Bay

name: Tung Po Kitchen
area: Wan Chai (2/F KONNECT, 303 Jaffe Road)
cuisine: Rowdy Cantonese dai pai dong / seafood
intro: A loud, famously fun Cantonese canteen where Cantopop blares and beer comes in bowls; it moved from North Point to Wan Chai in 2022.
reviews: Loved for its party atmosphere and showy service; some say the food matters less than the vibe and that it is very loud.
group_friendly: Very good for 10+ with big round tables, but book ahead. The booking policy could not be confirmed.
maps_query: Tung Po Kitchen 303 Jaffe Road Wan Chai

name: New Dim Siu Yi
area: North Point (G/F, 14 Tsat Tsz Mui Road; ~1 min from North Point MTR Exit B4)
cuisine: Cantonese dai pai dong / private-kitchen stir-fries
intro: A neighbourhood Cantonese spot in North Point for local-style seafood and stir-fries, away from the tourist circuit.
reviews: Praised for fresh seafood and generous dishes; some note inconsistent seasoning and oiliness.
group_friendly: Open 17:30–23:30, cash only. Booking advised; capacity for 10+ unknown. (A separate 店小二(東寶) is in the Java Road cooked-food centre.)
maps_query: New Dim Siu Yi 14 Tsat Tsz Mui Road North Point

name: Sing Kee
area: Central (Stanley Street)
intro: One of Central's last licensed open-air street-food stalls, serving wok-fried Cantonese dishes on folding tables in the street.
reviews: Fans praise the wok hei and the atmosphere; critics call it a tourist trap with hygiene issues and seafood that is not always fresh for the price.
group_friendly: Outdoor tables can be pushed together for groups. Cash only. Open Mon–Sat 11:00–15:00 and 18:00–23:00.
maps_query: Sing Kee Dai Pai Dong Stanley Street Central

name: Lin Heung Lau
area: Sheung Wan (G/F–2/F Tung Ning Building, 249–253 Des Voeux Road Central)
intro: A 100-year-old teahouse where dim sum still comes round on trolleys and you grab what you want.
must_order: Steamed chicken with rice in lotus leaf
reviews: Valued for authenticity and history; expect chaos, sharing tables and gruff service.
group_friendly: Hectic at peak times; groups should arrive early or ask about bookings. It moved from Wellington Street, Central, in April–May 2026.
maps_query: Lin Heung Lau 249 Des Voeux Road Central Sheung Wan

name: Luk Yu Tea House
area: Central (24 Stanley Street)
intro: Hong Kong's grand 1933 teahouse with ceiling fans, wood panels and waiters in white jackets, listed in the 2026 Michelin Guide.
reviews: Admired for its atmosphere and classic dim sum; frequent complaints are high prices and cold service toward non-regulars.
group_friendly: Booking strongly recommended; there are large tables over several floors. Open from 07:00.
maps_query: Luk Yu Tea House 24 Stanley Street Central

name: Tim Ho Wan (Central)
area: Central (Shop 12A, Level 1, Hong Kong Station / IFC Mall)
intro: The famous 'cheapest Michelin-starred dim sum' chain, a quick and inexpensive way to try classics.
reviews: Great value and reliable; complaints are queues (15+ min), rushed service and a shop that is hard to find inside the station.
group_friendly: No bookings and a queue system. 10+ will likely be split across tables.
maps_query: Tim Ho Wan Hong Kong Station IFC Mall

name: Maxim's Palace (City Hall)
area: Central (2/F Low Block, City Hall, 5 Edinburgh Place)
cuisine: Cantonese banquet-hall dim sum with trolleys
intro: A huge chandeliered banquet hall with harbour views, one of the last places with traditional dim sum trolleys.
reviews: Loved for the trolley experience and buzz; expect long waits at weekends and brusque service.
group_friendly: Very good for 10+ with round tables. Queue numbers are issued from opening; reservations are possible (OpenTable lists it). No closure or renovation news found.
maps_query: Maxim's Palace City Hall Central

name: Dim Sum Library
area: Admiralty (Shop 124, 1/F Pacific Place)
intro: A stylish, modern take on dim sum with truffle twists and tea-based cocktails, in a mall right above Admiralty MTR.
reviews: Reviews are mixed: some praise the creative dim sum and staff, others call it average for the price with slow service. It reopened after a renovation in spring 2026.
group_friendly: Book ahead (SevenRooms or OpenTable); it is busy at peak times. Workable for groups.
maps_query: Dim Sum Library Pacific Place Admiralty

name: Madame Fù – Grand Café Chinois
area: Central (Block 3, Tai Kwun, 10 Hollywood Road)
cuisine: Modern Cantonese / dim sum / afternoon tea
intro: A glamorous Chinese café inside the restored Tai Kwun police compound, known for dim sum, afternoon tea and its veranda bar.
reviews: Admired for its beautiful rooms; some say the food is pricey for what it is.
group_friendly: Has private rooms and handles big groups well; booking needed.
maps_query: Madame Fu Grand Cafe Chinois Tai Kwun

name: A Smoking Affair
area: Causeway Bay (27/F Soundwill Plaza II – Midtown)
cuisine: Hong Kong hotpot with private karaoke rooms
intro: Hotpot in neon-lit, 1970s Nathan Road-style rooms where you can sing karaoke privately while you eat, plus an outdoor terrace.
reviews: High ratings (4.8 on Tripadvisor) for the fun concept and broths; budget around HK$500–700 per person.
group_friendly: Excellent for 10+: 5–7 karaoke VIP rooms. Book ahead. Open until 2am.
maps_query: A Smoking Affair Soundwill Plaza II Causeway Bay

name: Lau Haa Hot Pot Restaurant
area: Causeway Bay (B/F & G/F, Block A, Lockhart House, 441 Lockhart Road)
intro: A basement hotpot joint dressed as a 1970s Hong Kong street, with neon signs and Cantopop.
reviews: Big portions and great nostalgic décor; common complaints are steep prices and limited English.

maps_query: Lau Haa Hot Pot Lockhart House 441 Lockhart Road

name: Kau Kee Restaurant
area: Central (21 Gough Street)
intro: A Michelin Bib Gourmand noodle shop famous for its beef brisket in clear or curry broth.

reviews: Outstanding brisket; complaints are 20–45 min queues, rushed and surly service, and cash only.
group_friendly: Not for groups: shared tables and a 15-minute turnover. Go in 2–4s. Closed Sundays.
maps_query: Kau Kee Restaurant Gough Street Central

name: Mak An Kee Noodle (Chung Kee)

group_friendly: Small and quick; not suitable for 10+. Open 10:30–20:00 (Sun to 19:00). Note: the Wellington Street shop is the separate Mak's Noodle (麥奀雲吞麵世家, 77 Wellington St).
maps_query: Mak An Kee Noodle 37 Wing Kut Street Central

name: Yuk Kin Fast Food

maps_query: Yuk Kin Fast Food 6 Tai Ping Shan Street Sheung Wan

name: Tak Yu Restaurant
area: Wan Chai (G/F, 17–18 St Francis Yard)

reviews: Cheap, nostalgic and tasty; occasional hygiene and service complaints.
group_friendly: Small; groups will be split. Mon–Sat 8:00–18:00, closed Sundays.
maps_query: Tak Yu Restaurant St Francis Yard Wan Chai

name: Samsen (Sheung Wan)

maps_query: Samsen 23 Jervois Street Sheung Wan

maps_query: El Taquero 119 Queen's Road East Wan Chai

Blue Room vs Green Room vibe
